script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

SARAH, 30s, wears a smart business suit. She sits at a table, sipping her coffee. Across the room, JAMES, 40s, enters. They make eye contact, both looking away quickly. Sarah puts her coffee down, gathering her things.

SARAH
(to herself)
I can't keep running.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LOBBY

Sarah exits the coffee shop, and James follows her from a distance. He catches up to her outside.

JAMES
Sarah, wait.

SARAH
(angrily)
Why are you here?

JAMES
(sincerely)
I want to talk. To apologize.

SARAH
(scoffs)
For what? You ruined my life!

JAMES
(hesitantly)
Yes, I made mistakes. But I've changed. I've spent years regretting what I did to you.

INT. PARK - DAY

They sit on a bench, surrounded by people enjoying the sun.

SARAH
You lied to me, James. You told me you loved me, and then you left me for someone else.

JAMES
(ashamed)
I was a coward. I didn't have the courage to face the truth. But I've been dealing with the guilt every day since.

SARAH
(frustrated)
You think an apology can make up for that?

JAMES
(determined)
No, but maybe it's a start. I want to make amends, to make things right between us.

INT. SARAH'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Sarah sits on her couch, holding a photo of her and James. She looks at it, then calls him.

SARAH
(on phone)
Fine. I'll see you tomorrow.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The next day, Sarah sits at the same table as James. They make small talk, catching up on each other's lives.

SARAH
(looking at him)
Why did you come back to me, James?

JAMES
(smiling)
Because I realized that the person I truly loved was you. And I couldn't live without the regret of losing you.

They share a moment of understanding, their eyes locked.

SARAH
(tearfully)
I forgive you, James.

JAMES
(gratefully)
Thank you, Sarah. I won't let you down again.

They hold hands, their connection stronger than before.

FADE OUT.

---

This screenplay follows the theme of forgiveness and the journey of two characters, Sarah and James, as they work through their past mistakes and rebuild their relationship. No guns, no violence, just raw emotion and the power of human connection.
